inc.cap: Anomalies that fire together are grouped into one correlated incident with a lifecycle — opening when the cluster trips and clearing once every member has settled back to normal. One incident, many signals.
inc.none_d: Anomalies that fire together would be grouped here as one event. Nothing correlated has tripped.

ribbon.cap: Each cell is one sample window, shaded by how far GPU util / VRAM / power / temperature sat from their own recent baseline. Click a hot cell to ask the local LLM what was running then.
ribbon.cap_host: Each cell is one sample window, shaded by how far CPU, RAM and load sat from their own recent baseline.
explain.st_generic: Local LLM unavailable — showing what the monitor saw around that moment instead.
vramfc.title: 🧠 VRAM headroom & ETA
vramfc.cap: Free VRAM is total minus what loaded models currently hold. The ETA fits VRAM-used over the last few hours; it only shows a time-to-full when the trend is credibly rising under load, otherwise it reads “stable”.

llm.no_resident: No models resident in VRAM right now — ollama unloads them after the keep-alive window.
llm.trend_thin: Not enough measurements yet — run a digest, ask the Copilot, or hit Quick benchmark a couple of times to build a trend.
llm.trend_aria: Tokens per second over the last {n} measurements: min {mn}, max {mx}, latest {cur}.

diag.fleet_meta: What the monitor can see on this hub, and how to enable anything that's missing. The dashboard keeps running even when optional pieces aren't mounted — no GPU required.
mcp.card_desc: A read-only MCP server is built in, so Claude — or any MCP client — can connect and explore this homelab with full dashboard parity, right down to what each model and container costs to run.
mcp.connect_hint: Connect with the Claude CLI (then ask it about your fleet):
alerts.intro: Push notifications when something noteworthy happens. Configured here — no env vars, no config files. Any channel (Discord, ntfy, or Telegram) can be used; all are optional. Alerts are edge-triggered (one ping per state change) so they don't spam.
alerts.enabled_label: Alerts enabled — turn the notifier on once a channel below is filled in.
alerts.ntfy_cap: Topic is required; server defaults to https://ntfy.sh. Self-hosted ntfy works too.
alerts.telegram_cap: Required with a bot token. Message your bot once, then read chat.id from getUpdates.
alerts.triggers: Triggers: container unhealthy/exited non-zero/dead, systemd unit failed, GPU VRAM pressure (free < PRESSURE_FREE_MB), GPU OOM events, and disks crossing the threshold above.
alerts.webhook_cap: Optional. We POST a small JSON envelope {source,level,title,detail,ts} — wire it into Home Assistant, n8n, a script, or Slack-incoming.
alerts.slack_cap: Optional. Posts a level-coloured message to a Slack channel via an incoming webhook.
alerts.slack_saved: A webhook is saved. Leave blank to keep it; type a new one to replace; type CLEAR and save to remove.
alerts.email_cap: Optional. Active once host, From, and To are filled in. Sends plain-text alerts via SMTP.
alerts.smtp_pass_saved: A password is saved. Leave blank to keep it; type a new one to replace; type CLEAR and save to remove.
rules.intro: Smarter alerts on top of the channels above. A rule watches a signal the dashboard already computes and fires through your channel when it crosses a line. Every rule is OFF until you enable it, with a per-rule cooldown so it never spams. Read-only — this only sends data out, it never changes the host.
rules.no_channel: No channel configured yet — add a Discord/ntfy/Telegram/webhook channel on the 🔔 Alerts page first.
maint.title: 🔕 Maintenance windows
maint.intro: Mute outbound alert notifications during a scheduled window — a nightly docker-pull restart cycle, or planned maintenance. Alerting is paused (not changed): an alarm that begins and ends inside a window never notifies, but anything still active when the window ends fires normally afterward. This never touches the host.
maint.none: No maintenance windows — alerts are never muted.
routes.title: 🔀 Notification routing
routes.intro: Send matching alerts to a specific channel instead of every channel. A route matches when the alert's subject (container/service/host/series/mount/check name) fits its pattern and its level is at or above the route's minimum. Routes are checked top-to-bottom; an alert goes to every matching route's channel.
routes.note: No routes = every alert goes to its rule's own channel (today's default). Routing only ever redirects matching alerts — it never drops them.
routes.none: No routes — alerts go to their rule’s channel (default).
rules.none: No rules yet — add one above.
costset.intro: Set your electricity price so the dashboard can turn power into money on the 💰 Costs page. Don't know your rates? Pick your country for a typical, editable estimate.
intg.intro: Push run/session data from Jupyter, Colab or Kaggle (or mirror MLflow) — each run comes back priced with the real GPU energy it used. Writes need the API key; the dashboard reads are open on your LAN.
intg.keys_cap: Create one key per machine/notebook so you can track and revoke each independently. Keys are stored hashed — the secret is shown once, at creation.
intg.mlflow_cap: Mirror runs from an MLflow tracking server — they appear under Runs with GPU cost attached. Synced every ~5 min.
backup.intro: Export your SQLite history, events, alert settings, and host registry — or restore a snapshot after a container recreate or disk move. SSH keys under /data/.ssh are not included; back those up separately if needed.
backup.note: Restore replaces all current database contents with the uploaded file. A safety copy of the previous database is kept alongside it as *.pre-restore-*.bak.
hosts.intro: Monitor your other machines from this hub — agentless, read-only, over SSH. Three quick steps: authorize the hub's key on a machine, add it here, then Test.
hosts.step1_t: Authorize this hub on the machine
hosts.step1_d: Run this on the machine you want to monitor so the hub can log in (read-only). Pick its operating system:
hosts.step2_d: A short name and its SSH target. Don't know the address? Scan your LAN for candidates.
hosts.step3_d: Hit Test on a host below — the checklist shows exactly what to fix for anything not yet working, with copy-paste commands for that machine's OS. Typo in a target? Click ✎ to edit it inline.
gpu.pergpu_cap: Live per-card utilisation, VRAM, power and temperature. The cards above pool VRAM and power across all GPUs.
gpu.vram_cap: Stacked = VRAM each service holds. Dashed = capacity. Red bands = VRAM pressure; ▼ markers = out-of-memory events.
costs.disabled: Set an electricity price in Settings → Costs to turn power into money.
costs.comp_cap: GPU power is measured (nvidia-smi); CPU/DRAM are measured via RAPL when readable. "Other" appears only if you set a baseline in Settings — wall power is never guessed.
costs.breakdown_cap: Click a row to drill into its power & cost over time. GPU split by VRAM share; CPU split by CPU-time share of the measured package power.
heat.title: 🗓️ Busy hours — when your lab burns power
heat.collecting: Collecting data — the busy-hours map fills in as history accumulates (about a day of samples).
heat.a11y_caption: Average power draw by day of week and hour of day. Higher is busier and more expensive.
heat.cap: Each cell is the average total draw (GPU + CPU + DRAM) for that local day-of-week and hour, over the chosen window. Colour scales by cost-rate when a tariff is set, otherwise by power. Sparse cells are dimmed — hover for the exact figures.
heat.bands_sub: busiest quarter vs quietest quarter of hours
exp.runs_sub: — pushed from your notebooks & MLflow, priced with real GPU energy
exp.runs_empty: No runs yet. Push one from Jupyter/Colab/Kaggle with the tiny client, or wire up MLflow — set it up in Settings → Integrations.
exp.train_sub: — training processes running now (no push needed)
exp.devtools_cap: Auto-discovered DS/AI web tools running on the hub. A 🟡 VRAM tag means a kernel/process is holding GPU memory — often a forgotten notebook squatting on VRAM.
exp.sess_cap: Contiguous GPU-busy periods reconstructed from power & utilisation history — each is a training run, batch job or inference burst. Energy is integrated from GPU power; cost uses your kWh price.
costset.tariff_cap: Powers the 💰 Costs page and the Power & cost cards from power history. Day & Night bills each sample at the night rate inside the window (it may cross midnight) and the day rate otherwise — leave the night price blank to use the single average. Leave the price blank to hide the cost cards.
costset.baseline_cap: GPU and CPU-package power are measured. Wall power is never guessed. Set a flat baseline here only if you want an "Other" band on the Costs chart for the rest of the box.
intg.colab_cap: Colab/Kaggle run in the cloud — point url at a Tailscale/ngrok address that reaches this hub.
net.talkers_cap: Total bytes each container moved over the selected range (its own network namespace).
security.cap: Read-only, agentless — no changes are made to any host. Items shown in grey (⚪) couldn't be read without elevated privileges on that machine.
models.section_cap: One panel per model server: its VRAM timeline (shared by the models it hosts) plus each model's own peak & average. A server is shown even while Idle (model unloaded / between requests), so nothing vanishes when VRAM is released. Recognised: Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, LocalAI, HF TGI/TEI, LoRAX, mistral.rs, Aphrodite, koboldcpp, tabbyAPI, text-generation-webui, LM Studio, xinference, OpenLLM, LiteLLM, GPUStack, Cortex/Jan, Ramalama, Nexa, Triton, Infinity, faster-whisper/Speaches, Whisper ASR webservice/WhisperX, Wyoming (HA voice), OpenedAI-Speech, Stable Diffusion (A1111/Forge/SD.Next), InvokeAI, ComfyUI.
footer.about:
Self-hosted & open source • single container • no Prometheus/Grafana required • history downsampled on read. GPU services attributed via /proc/<pid>/cgroup + the Docker API.
Ideas welcome — see CONTRIBUTING.md · issues & PRs always open.
hosts.prefilled: Prefilled — replace "user" with the SSH user, then Add host.
copilot.title: 🧠 Lab Copilot
copilot.card_desc: A plain-English read of your lab right now, written by a local LLM running on this host — no cloud. It summarises the live GPU, biggest model, disk-fill ETA, projected cost and any anomaly from the data the monitor already collects.
copilot.ask_ph: Ask about your lab… e.g. is anything overheating?
copilot.st_no_model: Model “{m}” is not pulled on this host — run: ollama pull {m}
copilot.st_unreachable: Local LLM not reachable — start ollama on this host to enable live summaries.
copilot.st_bad: The local LLM returned no text; showing the raw facts instead.
copilot.st_generic: Local LLM unavailable — showing the raw metrics instead.
copilot.inf_title: Estimated energy & cost this local generation burned
reco.title: ✅ Recommendations
reco.card_desc: A ranked, actionable to-do list derived from your lab's own live signals — disk-fill ETAs, VRAM headroom, cost trend, active incidents/anomalies, OOM kills and uptime. Each item carries a severity, the signal it's based on, and a concrete next step. Advice only — nothing here changes your host.
reco.allclear_d: No recommendations right now — disks, VRAM, cost, incidents and uptime all look healthy.
digest.title: 📬 Scheduled digest
digest.desc: Push a structured, plain-English brief to your alert channels on a schedule — an AI summary plus capacity, cost, fleet and anomaly sections. Off by default — needs a notification channel configured under Alerts.
digest.no_channel: No channel configured — set one under Alerts first.
cmdk.triage_all_healthy: All containers healthy — nothing to triage.
cmdk.triage_local_only: Container triage is available on the local host — switch to Local to triage.
imgupd.title: ⬆ Docker image-update awareness
imgupd.cap: Compares each running container's deployed image digest with the upstream registry's current tag digest (Docker Hub, GHCR, and other public v2 registries) and flags when a newer image exists. Awareness only — it NEVER pulls, runs, restarts or deletes anything. Heavily cached and bounded; off by default to avoid background registry traffic. Private/digest-pinned/local-only images show as "unknown".
imgupd.enable: Enable image-update checks — read-only registry queries on a slow cadence.
mqtt.title: 🏠 Home Assistant / MQTT (push)
mqtt.cap: Publish your key metrics to an MQTT broker with Home Assistant auto-discovery — the lab shows up as native HA sensors (GPU util/VRAM/power/temp, total power, cost MTD/projected, anomaly, uptime) grouped under one device. Publish-only: the monitor never subscribes and never controls anything. Off by default.
mqtt.enable: Enable MQTT publishing — off until a broker host is filled in below.
mqtt.pass_saved: A password is saved. Leave blank to keep it; type a new one to replace; type CLEAR and save to remove.
mqtt.status_unconf: Enabled but no broker host set.
